subject: Request: temporary SLA variance for late async job completions
messages:
From: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Job completions delayed last night - data attached

Ben / Redwood team,

We noticed ~12% of our nightly async jobs completed outside the 4 hour window last night. Impact: (1) downstream reports delayed, (2) some customer workflows retried and produced duplicate records. Attached are a few job logs and the job manifest for 2025-06-29. Can you confirm root cause and whether you can provide a short-term SLA variance while we evaluate idempotency tweaks on our side?

Thanks,
Sarah King
Sr. Engineering Manager, Data Platform
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_job_samples_20250629.log (text/log)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Job completions delayed last night - data attached

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the logs. We dug in and saw a transient autoscaler oscillation combined with a cache warm-up spike that elongated tail latency for a subset of long-running batch partitions. Early hypothesis: safe-retry behavior on Acme's side combined with the late completions caused some duplicate downstream work.

Short-term proposal from our side:
- We can offer a temporary SLA variance for the nightly async job completion window: extend the 4h guarantee to a 6h window for the next 3 production nights, effective immediately.
- During the variance period Redwood will apply an emergency mitigation: pin dedicated batch workers for Acme to reduce autoscale churn and enable a conservative batching policy.
- We'll also enable a prefix/KV cache pre-warm for the top 20 job keys to reduce long-tail.

Requesting ACME confirmation so we can schedule the changes for tonight. If agreed, we'll produce an amendment doc and provide a credit plan if reoccurrence beyond the variance occurs.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: sla_variance_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal PDF)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: tech review and safe-retry guidance

Ben / Aditya —

Checked the job traces. Two technical notes for the amendment:
1) Idempotency surface: recommend Acme add an external idempotency key for the job payloads (per-job UUID) so retries from downstream can be de-duped.
2) Safe-at-least-once plan: while variance is in effect, we'll enable a 30-minute de-duplication window in the router and add an explicit Retry-After header for in-flight partitions to guide client retries.

If legal needs a credit cap we should propose 5% of the monthly committed spend as an upper bound for the variance period. Also suggest we include rollback criteria: if late completion rate >5% during variance we auto-trigger a post-mortem and additional credits.

Grace O'Connor
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Formal variance proposal and action plan (effective tonight)

Sarah —

Per our calls, please find the agreed short-term plan below: 
1) SLA variance: Redwood will temporarily relax the nightly async job completion SLA from 4h -> 6h for a 3-night window (2025-07-01 to 2025-07-03).
2) Technical mitigations (applied 2025-07-01 22:00 UTC): pin dedicated batch workers, conservative batching config, and prefix cache pre-warm for top 20 keys.
3) Retry/idempotency guidance: see Grace's notes — we will add a 30-minute router de-dupe window and emit Retry-After headers. Acme to implement per-job UUIDs for full dedupe end-to-end.
4) Credit and escalation terms: if >5% of jobs breach the new 6h window during variance, Redwood will issue a credit up to 5% of the monthly committed spend for Acme (per deal ACME-12345) and initiate a joint post-mortem.

Please reply with a one-line approval and we'll formalize the amendment. If you want additional guardrails (e.g., finer-grained affected-job lists) we can include those in the doc.

Thanks — ready to flip the switch tonight on your confirmation.

—Ben
From: Sarah King <sarah.king@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com, ingest-team@datariver.io
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Formal variance proposal and action plan (effective tonight)

Ben / team —

Thanks for the quick triage and clear plan. We approve the temporary variance (4h -> 6h) for the 3-night window and authorize Redwood to apply the mitigations tonight. We'll begin adding per-job UUIDs to our ingest pipeline this week — target to complete within two sprints. Please proceed and share the amendment as a short DocuSign for our procurement team.

Sarah
